newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudanese demonstrate against U.N. sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese demonstrate against U.N. sanctions.

text.p: Sudanese protested in Khartoum on Thursday against an air embargo the United Nations has threatened to impose on Sudan.

"Our country has never known terrorism not has it shown any signs of fundamentalism. But we understand that if pressures continue against us, then for every action there is a reaction," Vice President Al-Zubair Mohammed Salih told the state-organised demonstration. He did not elaborate.

The United Nations has slapped limited travel and diplomatic sanctions on Sudan for failing to extradite to Egypt or Ethiopia three gunmen accused of trying to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa in June 1995.

The Security Council on August 16 also imposed an air embargo on Sudan but delayed putting it into effect for at least three months depending on a U.N. report on whether Khartoum was complying with the council's demands.
Sudan says the men are not within its borders and that there is no concrete evidence that it harbours the suspects.

The United States has labelled Sudan's Islamist government "terrorist" and most of the neighbours of the African state accuse it of harbouring and training rebels trying to overthrow their more secular regimes.
